newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Franchise sees 1997 loss equaling 1996.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Franchise sees 1997 loss equaling 1996.

text.p: U.S. Franchise Systems Inc said on Monday that it expects its loss for 1997 will be about equal to the loss reported for 1996.
Mike Leven, president and chief executive officer, said the projection is based on current schedules for property openings and revisions on its loan-conduit outlook and "American Dream" programs.
"In addition, we believe our first profitable period will be the final quarter of 1998, unless we complete an acquisition, a strategy that the company continues to pursue aggressively," he said.
U.S. Franchise Systems, which went public in October 1996, reported a pro forma net loss of $0.66 per share for 1996. It reported an actual net loss for the year of $6.591 million or $0.75 a share.
For the first quarter of 1997, it said it signed 55 franchise agreements and had 242 total net franchises sold since the company's inception in August 1995.

After terminations and openings, it said it ended the latest quarter with 214 Microtel Inns and 28 Hawthorne Suites units sold. It said it executed 45 Mircotel and 10 Hawthorne franchise agreements during the quarter.
Five Microtel Inns opened, bringing the chain's total properties to 33, it said.
It said a lower number of franchisees than it had anticipated had chosen to turn to US Funding Corp, its financing subsidiary, for construction and permanent first mortgages.
"If this trend continues, fees earned through US Funding will be significantly below our expectations," it said.

It said that the lone developer under the American Dream program, which was developed to allow Microtel Inns to be acquired on lease-purchase basis, wants to evaluate performance of the initial 10 units before committing to additional construction.

"As a result, we have reduced our forecast for both open units and sales for the remainder of 1997," it said. The company expects to open five to nine additional American Dream properties this year and remain hopeful that the program eventually will reach its original goals, Leven noted.
